statements.text: USFK's current approach is to implement human/machine teaming into the Joint Planning Process. We created a digital planning branch to accomplish this mission need with four distinct efforts: Data Governance, Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning enhancements, Automation, and Partnering. [...] Our overall methodology is to produce quick wins as we march towards decision dominance that is made possible when we leverage Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning in our planning.
statements.context: Written testimony to the House Armed Services Committee on U.S. military posture in the Indo-Pacific, responding to questions about how USINDOPACOM harnesses emerging technologies for planning.

statements.text: Dario Amodei, has publicly fielded the idea of a token tax where a small percentage of language model revenues could go to the government to help offset the economic disruptions AI could cause [...] To me, it reflects a bigger principle that AI companies have a responsibility to help address the societal costs their technologies could bring. [...] Should companies like Anthropic be expected to directly invest in the infrastructure that they rely on so that we can actually increase our capacity, as well reinforcing the environmental and public systems that are being stretched to support the growth of AI?
statements.context: Ms. Tokuda questions a witness at a hearing titled 'Algorithms and Authoritarians: Why U.S. AI Must Lead,' asking about public-private burden sharing for AI infrastructure costs.

statements.text: We know that China is investing significant resources and assets to achieve its 2030 AI world leader goal, and meanwhile here at home, we say we want to win the AI race, but the current administration proposed gutting the very institutions that both give us an edge and protect us from intrusion.
statements.context: Congressional hearing on U.S. AI leadership and competition with China, where the member questions a witness about the impact of proposed budget cuts to NIST and CISA.

statements.text: Mr. Beall, your testimony makes clear that artificial superintelligence _ ASI _ is one of the largest existential threats that we face right now, and many experts in the field also recognize that AGI _ artificial general intelligence _ is a precursor to that risk.
statements.context: Congressional hearing titled 'Algorithms and Authoritarians: Why U.S. AI Must Lead,' where Rep. Tokuda questions panelists on existential AI risks and governance.

statements.text: Despite the fact we are in the middle of a global AI race, the Trump Administration wants to gut the very institutions that give us a technological edge. We should be increasing, not cutting, funding that allows us to compete internationally and protect ourselves domestically. https://t.co/ykguIPO5Bf

With regard to standing up to China, I introduced an amendment requiring congressional approval before advanced AI chips, critical to our most sophisticated weapons and intelligence systems, could be exported to Beijing. It was blocked.
statements.context: House floor debate during the FY2026 NDAA amendment process, where Rep. Tokuda lists amendments she submitted that were blocked by the Rules Committee.

statements.text: I am definitely on team guardrails.

We've seen all of these movies. It does not end well. It does not end well where, at the end of the day, we're not just competing against each other, we're actually competing against an entity, an 'it,' if you will, an AI system.

We have to make sure that we are constantly moving forward with this approach versus all hands off, let's just get to the finish line first and then we'll figure it out, because the bottom line is once we get to AGI, it's over. It's over. We've lost the ability to control any such entity if we haven't first built in the protections and guardrails required to even get us to that point.
We need a full, impartial review to determine if AI has already harmed or jeopardized lives in the war with Iran,
statements.venue: The Independent, statement on military AI use

statements.text: We cannot outsource our conscience to a computer, especially when lives are on the line,
statements.venue: Honolulu Star-Advertiser interview on Army AI testing

statements.text: AI has the potential to automate time-intensive tasks, strengthen supply chains and operational planning, and help piece together battlefield intelligence far faster than humans alone,

statements.text: Those are not unreasonable demands; they are basic safeguards,

statements.text: Mr. Chan, in your testimony, I really appreciated your analysis that China is essentially looking beyond AGI. [...] I often say in this committee that sometimes I feel like we are playing checkers and they are on 3D chess many times because it is not just about getting to AGI.
statements.context: Congressional hearing on China's campaign to steal America's AI edge, with Ms. Tokuda questioning a witness about US counter-strategy.

statements.text: So some kind of global framework. Should we not just be looking at ourselves but be concerned about the global instability and maybe perhaps trying to go back to providing both that leadership and that direction in terms of the smart regulation and guidelines that we should have as the world develops towards AGI and, quite frankly, ASI right behind it?
statements.context: US House hearing on China's efforts to steal American AI technology, with the member questioning witnesses about regulatory and international governance gaps.

statements.text: Thank you. I know my time is up, but I absolutely agree we need to invest more, support more, encourage more open source on that front. If we look at many of the AI that is out there, you have got China DNA imprinted in everything, and that was very strategically done and intentionally done. Thank you, Mr. Chair. I yield back.
statements.context: Remarks by Ms. Tokuda during a congressional hearing titled "China's Campaign to Steal America's AI Edge."

statements.text: Congress has an important role to play in ensuring artificial intelligence is developed responsibly. AI has enormous potential to improve healthcare, education, agriculture, and emergency response, but innovation must be paired with clear safeguards that protect people. [...] We don’t have to choose between innovation and responsible oversight. We can encourage groundbreaking technology while protecting consumers, workers, and our national security.

Mahalo to the students, faculty, and staff at UH Maui College for inviting me to talk story over pizza. 🍕

We had a thoughtful conversation about the issues on their minds, from AI and the growing power of big tech to women's health and reproductive rights and school voucher court decisions. I’m always grateful for the chance to be with our students, hear what they’re thinking, and talk about the challenges shaping their lives and our communities.

If the United States gives our very best AI chips to China, it would exponentially increase their capacity to dominate the AI race,[...] We must not let that happen. Retaining the most advanced AI chips for domestic use, along with allies and partners, is an effective way to slow down China’s AI progress and strengthen America’s economic and national security advantages.
